name: Hashabniah
title: Levite who participated in the renewal of the covenant
summary: Hashabniah was a Levite who lived after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of those who took part in public prayer and confession, as well as in sealing the covenant with God. His role was connected to the spiritual renewal of the people of Israel under Nehemiah's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Participation in public prayer and confession
keyEvents.description: Hashabniah was among the Levites who stood up and cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God during the great public gathering for prayer in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The people's confession of sin
keyEvents.description: As part of the group of Levites, Hashabniah led the people in a long prayer that reviewed God's faithfulness and Israel's repeated sins throughout history.

keyEvents.title: Sealing of the covenant
keyEvents.description: Hashabniah was among those who placed their seal on the written covenant in which the people committed themselves to follow God's law.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding and organizing Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: In connection with the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls, a Hashabnia (or his son) is mentioned as leader over half a district, showing the family's leading position in society.

keyEvents.title: Renewal of worship in the temple
keyEvents.description: As a Levite, Hashabnia contributed to restoring orderly worship in the temple after the exile, in line with the reforms of Ezra and Nehemiah.
